replaceSection.heading: GLOSSARY
items: **Artificial Source of Light:** A source of light made by people, such as a bulb or torch.
**Drug:** Any externally administered substance which modifies or alters the rate of metabolic reactions in the body.
**Evaporation:** The process by which water changes into water vapour and disappears into the air, often with the help of heat from sunlight.
**Freezing:** The change of state from liquid to solid when heat is removed.
**Gas:** A state of matter that spreads out to fill all the space available.
**Insolubility:** The inability of a substance to dissolve in water.
**Light Energy:** A form of energy that makes things bright and helps us see.
**Liquid:** A state of matter that flows and takes the shape of its container.
**Matter:** Anything that has a mass and occupies space.
**Melting:** The change of matter from solid to liquid when heat is added.
**Mixture:** A combination of two or more substances mixed together.
**Natural Source of Light:** A source of light that occurs in nature, such as the Sun or stars.
**Photosynthesis:** The process by which plants use sunlight to make their own food and grow.
**Pulse:** A wave of pressure created in the arteries by a heartbeat.
**Pure Substance:** A material made of only one type of substance.
**Solid:** A state of matter that has a fixed shape and size.
**Solubility:** The ability of a substance to dissolve in water.
**Sublimation:** The change of state from solid to gas without becoming a liquid first.
**Withdrawal symptom:** Symptoms or signs that an individual experiences when they discontinue using a drug they are addicted to.
